title: Which way does S move?

readouts.l: Quantity supplied at the own price

predict.q: The government adds a tax of 1 on every unit sold. What happens to the supply curve?

options.fb: A tax raises the cost of selling each unit, so firms offer less at every price: S shifts left.
The tax adds 1 to the cost of every unit, so S moves up by exactly 1 at every quantity: less is supplied at every price.
The good's own price has not changed yet; a tax changes the conditions of supply, so the curve shifts.

options.s: No change: buyers pay the tax
options.fb: Who finally pays is a separate question (incidence, M11). The tax is paid by sellers to the government, so S shifts.

task: Move the **tax per unit** slider and watch S. Then try **input costs** and **number of firms**.

target.do: Move the tax per unit slider from 0 to 1, then press Check.

takeaway: Anything that raises cost per unit shifts S **left**; anything that lowers it shifts S **right**.
explore: Input costs up → S left; more firms → S right; the own price only slides the point along S.
